mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as businesses and consumers react to reduced output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer spending, which is a strong indicator of economic growth and typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals strong economic growth coupled with a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
